incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Articles 287-2 through 287-64 (Yuhan Hoesa Limited Liability Company) together with Articles 169 through 219 on general company formation and registration; Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 4 through 6; Value-Added Tax Act, Article 5; and the Corporate Registration Act (Beobin Deunggi Beop)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registry Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office (for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registry Office; electronic filings may be made through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Registration Application (Beop-in Seongnip Deung-gi Sinsu-seo) accompanied by the Articles of Incorporation and supporting capital payment instruments
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa. Each member must, however, fully pay the agreed contribution before or concurrently with the incorporation registration, and no part of the paid contribution may be withdrawn, lent, or set off before registration is completed. In-kind contributions require a court-appointed appraiser unless all members are solvent and the Commercial Act exemption applies. For non-resident members, capital must be transferred into a Korean foreign-exchange bank account and reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; the company obtains a Foreign Investment Report Certificate. A blocked escrow account is not statutorily mandated for this service-only entity.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF YUHANGHOESA

WHEREAS, the incorporators have resolved to organize YUHANGHOESA (the 'Company') as a Yuhan Hoesa limited liability company under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, with the business scope restricted to civil-infrastructure CAD drafting, structural drafting, and Building Information Modeling (BIM) coordination services performed on an offshore outsourcing basis for non-Korean clients;

WHEREAS, the Articles of Incorporation authorize the appointment of directors and provide for the organizational acts required to complete statutory incorporation and governance;

WHEREAS, the persons whose names appear on the attached attendance roster constitute all initial members and directors entitled to take organizational action; and

WHEREAS, all statutory notice requirements have been waived by unanimous written consent of the members and directors;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. Adoption of Organizational Documents and Share Capital Subscription. RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation, the register of members, and the contribution schedule set forth in Annex A are hereby ratified and adopted in full. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the entire authorized initial membership contributions in the amount of [●] Korean Won be subscribed by the members appearing on the register, and that every member shall cause the full amount of his or her contribution to be paid into the Company’s designated bank account or into the capital payment account maintained in the Company’s name prior to the filing of the incorporation registration. No subscriber may withdraw, lend, offset, or recover any contributed amount before registration is perfected, and the bank’s original capital payment certificate shall be attached to the registration application.

2. Adoption of Registered Office. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be located at [●], Republic of Korea, and that such address is adopted as the statutory seat of the Company for service of process, tax notices, and all government communications. The Representative Director is instructed to maintain the office-use proof and, where the office is leased, to place the lessor’s written consent in the corporate records.

3. Banking Authorization. RESOLVED, that the Representative Director and the Chief Financial Officer are authorized, jointly as to any single transaction exceeding [●] KRW and individually below such threshold, to open, operate, and close domestic and foreign-currency accounts at [●] Bank or any other Financial Supervisory Service-licensed bank; to sign bank mandates, account applications, anti-money-laundering declarations, wire transfer instructions, SWIFT instructions, Wise corporate settlement instructions, and other payment-rail documents; and to appoint sub-authorized signatories in accordance with the board-approved banking resolution.

4. Appointment of Statutory Officers. RESOLVED, that [●] be and is hereby appointed Representative Director, [●] be and is hereby appointed Chief Financial Officer and internal director, [●] be and is hereby appointed Company Secretary, and [●] be retained as statutory auditor if and as required by the Commercial Act or the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies for the relevant fiscal year; otherwise, the audit appointment shall be deferred to the annual members’ meeting.

5. Filing and Registration Authority. RESOLVED, that the officers and counsel of the Company are authorized to prepare, execute, submit, correct, and retrieve all incorporation registration papers, to pay all court registry taxes and education surtaxes, to obtain the certificate of incorporation and corporate seal certificate, to make any foreign investment report required under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and to obtain the business registration certificate from the National Tax Service. All acts performed or to be performed by these persons in good faith in connection with the Company’s formation are hereby ratified, approved, and confirmed.

6. Effective Date and Secretary Certification. RESOLVED FURTHER, that this resolution is effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until altered or revoked by a subsequent board resolution; that no third-party dealing with the Company shall be required to inquire into the authority of any signatory named above; and that the Company Secretary is directed to place these minutes and required attachments in the corporate minute book and to certify this instrument as a true and complete record.

CERTIFIED TRUE THIS ____ day of ______________, 20____.

By: _________________________________
Name:
Title: Representative Director / Company Secretary

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of South Korea; online portal: HomeTax (hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a domestic Korean LLC (Yuhan Hoesa), the entity must register with the National Tax Service (NTS) within 10 days of commencing business. The procedure involves: (1) preparing the certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, and proof of business address; (2) submitting the Business Registration Application (사업자등록신청서) to the local district tax office; (3) providing the corporate seal registration certificate and identification of the representative; (4) receiving the Business Registration Number (사업자등록번호) which serves as both the TIN and VAT ID. For foreign non-resident entities, a tax representative must be appointed in Korea to handle filings and communications with the NTS. The application can be filed online via HomeTax or in person at the district tax office.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No threshold; mandatory registration for any taxable business activity (KRW 0)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic tax invoice issuance and submission via the HomeTax system for all B2B transactions. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS within 10 days after the end of the month in which the supply occurs. The system employs digital signatures and validation to prevent fraud. For B2C transactions, a cash receipt system is mandatory for retail businesses.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Services supplied to a non-resident and used outside Korea qualify for 0% VAT. For engineering and design services (including BIM and structural drafting), the place of supply is deemed to be where the recipient is located if the recipient is a business (B2B). The service must be performed for a foreign client and the benefit must be received outside Korea.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties for fraudulent or unverified export zero-rating include additional tax of up to 40% of the evaded VAT, interest on unpaid tax, and potential criminal prosecution for tax evasion. The NTS may retrospectively claw back the zero-rated VAT and impose penalties if documentation is incomplete or false.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the overarching foreign exchange policy authority.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-floating exchange rate regime for the KRW, with current-account transactions largely open under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Capital-account flows require advance registration or ex-post reporting through a domestic foreign exchange bank. For a Yuhan Hoesa LLC receiving equity investment and paying overseas engineering costs, neither a minimum capital requirement nor a blanket FX license is imposed, but every inbound/outbound transfer must be associated with a valid foreign exchange purpose code. KRW remains a partially restricted offshore currency; non-resident bank accounts and settlement between non-residents in KRW are limited, which pushes most treasury operations to be structured in USD or KRW through licensed domestic institutions. Profit remittance is legal after corporate taxes are filed; dividends are paid in KRW and converted to foreign currency through the entity's settlement bank, subject to submission of audited financial statements, dividend minutes, and tax payment certificates. Export proceeds from BIM and CAD services are treated as service export earnings, must be collected within six months, and can be held in a foreign currency account without forced surrender, though a bank receipt and service contract are mandatory for VAT and corporate tax purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, service export proceeds (including CAD/BIM deliverables) must be received in Korea within six months from the invoice due date or performance completion; there is no mandatory conversion ratio, but all receipts must be credited to a foreign exchange account and reported to the foreign exchange bank. Any delay exceeding six months requires BOK approval.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (DDA with FDI purpose code)
Settlement and Foreign Exchange Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury rail. Wise is a licensed e-money institution abroad but not a licensed deposit-taking bank in South Korea; it cannot open a corporate KRW operating account or provide a legal domestic settlement account for tax registration or FDI capital verification. It may be used only as a secondary payout channel for non-regulated low-value invoices where the recipient's bank accepts foreign fintech transfers; all statutory capital flows must move through domestic Tier-1 banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: South Korean AML/FTA regulations require that account opening for a foreign-invested company be validated with an in-person interview of the representative director and ultimate beneficial owner at the bank branch unless the bank explicitly accepts a remote video/consular-verification procedure. For a Yuhan Hoesa with foreign directors, at least one natural-person director or an authorized officer with a notarized apostilled POA must attend physically in Seoul; remote opening alone is not a statutory right and is treated as an enhanced-risk exception.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership opacity or mismatch between ultimate beneficial owners and account signatories.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, company registry extracts, notarized and apostilled personal ID/passport copies, three months bank reference from the home jurisdiction, organizational chart, and a written UBO declaration with ownership percentages.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection for FDI where the funds are not traceable to the investor's own account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Equity subscription agreement, board resolution, audited or certified translated financial statements, bank transaction history showing funds from the investor's own account rather than third-party cash, plus income tax or wealth tax evidence proving legitimate origin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering indicators in CAD/BIM transactions where invoices are generic or valuation is non-verifiable.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed service contracts with BIM scope and deliverables, milestone-based invoicing with timesheets or BIM file hash/version logs, signed acceptance certificates from the Korean counterparty, technical specification of CAD outputs, and matching SWIFT MT103 records for each settlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident entity with no demonstrable tax or operational substance in Korea, creating a shell profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Seat lease agreement or virtual office contract in Korea, payroll records of local employees, utility bills, corporate income tax receipts, VAT registration certificate, and board minutes showing substantive management decisions made in Korea.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must instruct a SWIFT MT103 from its home bank to the Korean entity's designated foreign currency account at a Tier-1 domestic bank, using the statutory FDI equity acquisition purpose code reported under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Upon credit, the domestic bank issues a certificate of foreign exchange acquisition; the entity then completes capital verification against paid-in capital and files the foreign investment notification through KOTRA or the domestic bank. All supporting documents must be retained for tax, VAT, and offshore audit purposes.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For payments to offshore engineering partners, subcontractors, or software licensing vendors, use SWIFT MT103 for service fees and smaller disbursements. For project-linked civil infrastructure material purchases, use Commercial Letters of Credit. For counterparties in emerging markets where documentary trust is weaker, use Documentary Collections (D/P or D/A). Each disbursement must be coded with the appropriate FX transaction purpose code and supported by the underlying service contract, milestone certificate, or import declaration.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore forward FX contracts with domestic Tier-1 banks for trade-backed flows
FX options with delegated underlying exposure approved by the bank
Cross-currency swaps for long-term project borrowings
Onshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only through licensed banks with any non-deliverable KRW positions strictly tied to real trade exposure
Currency swap arrangements for infrastructure project capital expenditure with documented exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and financial statements attachment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By March 31 of the calendar year following the fiscal year end (December 31 assumed); if the entity is subject to external audit, the deadline is extended to April 30 of the same year under the Corporate Tax Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 20% additional tax on the unpaid corporate tax amount under the Framework Act on National Taxes, plus daily interest at 0.022% per day on underpaid tax. Persistent non-filing and non-operation may lead to tax collection enforcement and administrative strike-off of the company by the Commercial Registry after sustained dormancy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax on Corporate Income return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Metropolitan City, City or Provincial Tax Authority of the head office jurisdiction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the filing/payment deadline of the corporate income tax; therefore by April 30 for the standard December 31 fiscal year, or May 31 if the corporate return was extended to April 30.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late filing or underpayment exposes the company to a 20% additional tax on the unpaid local income tax, plus daily delinquency interest of 0.022%. Repeated default may result in enforced collection against corporate assets and possible administrative dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax (VAT) semi-annual statutory return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (electronic filing through HomeTax system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For the first half of the fiscal year (January 1 to June 30): file and pay by July 25. For the second half (July 1 to December 31): file and pay by January 25 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing attracts a 10% additional tax on the unpaid VAT (20% for negligent understatement; 30% for fraudulent evasion) plus daily interest of 0.022% on amounts unpaid. Criminal penalties may apply for tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Regular Members' Meeting and approval of financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company records, minutes and member register; filing of required resolutions to the District Court Commercial Registry if amendments to articles or changes in managers/directors occur
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The regular members' meeting must be held and the financial statements approved within three months after the end of the fiscal year; therefore on or before March 31 for a December 31 year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the meeting and approve financial statements by the statutory deadline subjects responsible directors/officers to court-imposed administrative fines (up to KRW 20 million, approximately USD 15,400). Continued non-observance of statutory formalities may count toward the court's administrative strike-off threshold for dormant entities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and audited financial statements (if the statutory threshold is triggered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the DART electronic disclosure system, and submission to the members' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The independent certified public accountant must deliver the audited financial statements and audit report to the company by April 30 for a December 31 fiscal year; after approval at the regular members' meeting, the report must be filed with the Financial Supervisory Service within two weeks of approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file the external audit report with the FSS within the statutory window may result in an administrative fine up to KRW 30 million (approximately USD 23,100) under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. If no auditor is engaged despite the threshold being met, the company and its officers are exposed to criminal fines and a suspended designation of the external auditor by the Securities and Futures Commission.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registry change registration after annual meeting or after triggering corporate events
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: District Court Commercial Registry having jurisdiction over the company's head office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in directors/managers, registered capital, articles of incorporation, the registered business office, or other registered matters must be filed with the Commercial Registry within 14 days after the relevant change takes effect (including changes resolved at the annual members' meeting).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late registration exposes the company to an administrative fine under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act, generally up to KRW 500,000 (approximately USD 385), plus an additional daily penalty for continued non-compliance. Failure to file registered changes over an extended period is a factor supporting court-ordered administrative strike-off of a dormant company.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Korean Act on External Audit of Stock Companies (as amended, applicable to fiscal years starting on or after 2020), an independent audit by a certified public accountant is mandatory for: (i) all companies listed or intended to be listed on a Korean stock exchange; (ii) non-listed companies with total assets of KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million) or more at the end of the preceding fiscal year; (iii) non-listed companies that are deemed public-interest entities by Presidential Decree, including financial institutions, insurance companies, securities companies, mutual savings banks and collective investment operators, regardless of asset size; and (iv) certain companies with total assets between KRW 8 billion and KRW 12 billion that additionally satisfy designated revenue or employee headcount tests prescribed by the Enforcement Decree. An external audit is not required solely by headcount for ordinary private limited liability companies below the asset threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: The governing accounting framework for a South Korean Yuhan Hoesa (limited liability company) is Korean GAAP (General Accounting Standards) issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. For small and medium-sized entities, the 'Korean Accounting Standards for Small and Medium-Sized Entities' may be applied. If the company is subject to external audit and meets the criteria for a public-interest entity, Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) are mandatory. For domestic non-listed companies that do not fall within the K-IFRS mandate, Korean GAAP remains the accepted framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a general standalone annual UBO filing for a private domestic Yuhan Hoesa at the commercial registry. Beneficial ownership confirmation is event-driven and is performed through mandatory financial institution authentication under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality. Additionally, if the entity is a foreign-invested company under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, any change in foreign investment ownership, including share transfers, must be reported to the competent authority through a designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days of the change. For all entities, the annual regular members' meeting must reconcile the member register (company register) with the actual shareholding; transfers of membership interests are effective against third parties only when the transfer is recorded in the member register. Any change in statutory register particulars (directors, managers, registered office, or members if relevant under the articles) must be registered with the Commercial Registry within 14 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 - USD 3,200 per annum for a registered office address, agent correspondence handling, secretarial and registered agent services in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - USD 18,000 per annum for a licensed certified public accountant audit of a Korean non-listed Yuhan Hoesa conducting BIM and structural drafting services, depending on the complexity of its transactions and the use of K-IFRS versus Korean GAAP SME reporting
